evidence.note: Agent front-loaded downloading the three pinned vendored libraries and noted 'their hashes exactly match the verifier requirements' — awareness of the exact-path/exact-hash fatal gate early.
Ran sha256sum on all three static files as a concrete recomputed-hash check against the pinned digests — genuine verification rather than assumption of the most unforgiving gate.
Verified CSP/security headers present on the home UI, satisfying the strict-CSP gate and checking it before finishing.

Final submission summary lists hashes, headers, seed data as satisfied, but never mentions verifying the purple brand palette, the allowed compose button label, offline runtime serving, or an anti-cheat surface audit — several fatal gates left unaddressed/unverified.

reasoning: The agent identified and satisfied the most obvious fatal gates — exact pinned static paths/versions and strict CSP — and even verified the hashes with a concrete sha256sum recompute and inspected headers, which is above the level-5 'checking most' bar for those gates. But it did not systematically enumerate the full kill-switch set: the purple palette, allowed button label, offline runtime confirmation, the harbor-canary strip caveat, and the anti-cheat surface (Node artifacts, forbidden strings) are never triaged or verified. This falls squarely at the 5 anchor — major fatal gates satisfied and mostly checked — short of the explicit cost/fatality triage and full-surface verification of level 8.
